review_notes: I read all of lines 1–76. The file declares three private instances (tailNonempty, tailDirected, tailFiltered) and one theorem, isIso_restrictedGlobalSectionsComparison. It has no simp lemmas, simp attributes, simp sets, or simp calls. The proof is a direct `rw` chain followed by `exact`. The only lemmas it uses are colimit_ι_restrictedGlobalSectionsComparison and chosenLimitIso_inv_projection, from SheafCohomology/NativeCylinderComparison.lean, and colimit_ι_nativeGlobalSectionsComparison, from SheafCohomology/NativeLimitGlobalSections.lean. Any change to their simp or reassoc attributes would belong in those files, not here. I grepped their uses. The other files also apply them with `rw` after manual `← Category.assoc`. Making them simp or reassoc lemmas might shorten the proofs. I could not justify that as a concrete improvement, because the lemmas have a nontrivial composite shape and carry an `eqToHom` cast. The theorem is also not a simp-shaped rewrite rule: it is a conditional `IsIso` fact with hypotheses that simp could not discharge. I found no simp-interface defect in this file. I could not run Lean, so I could not test whether the other files' lemmas would work as simp lemmas.
